title: Lego bottom-up ruthenium wordlines with no CMP
idea: Random stimulus 'Lego': pieces snap on only where they belong. Grow the buried wordline by area-selective ALD/CVD of Ru (or Mo) from a seeded trench bottom, with the oxide top surface blocked by a vapor-dosed small-molecule inhibitor, so metal fills bottom-up to the exact recess height: no overburden, CMP, wet recess etch or post-CMP brush clean.
why: Deletes the slurry and post-CMP clean water of the wordline loop (>10x for that module) and removes tungsten (China ~80%); a lower-resistance wordline also allows a lower boosted voltage (fact 10).

title: Bonsai pillars: grow vertical channels instead of etching them
idea: Random stimulus 'bonsai': shape the growth rather than carve the wood. Form vertical access channels by selective epitaxy upward from bitline-contact seeds through a patterned oxide template made with one low-AR etch, so there is no 60:1 silicon etch, no etch-polymer wet strip and no damaged sidewall.
why: Deletes the high-AR etch-clean-rinse loop (>10x less water for the pillar module) and yields damage-free channel sidewalls with fewer interface traps, attacking the leakage tail at its source (fact 3).

title: Dry-erase resist patterns the array without developer baths
idea: Random stimulus 'dry-erase marker': mark and wipe with no liquid. Pattern the access-device critical layers (active area, buried wordline, storage contact) with vapor-deposited metal-oxide EUV resist that is dry-developed and stripped in plasma, so there is no spin coat, TMAH develop, DI rinse or wet strip.
why: Removes the track's develop/rinse water and the wet strips for the 5-7 array critical layers (>10x less water on those litho loops) and lowers line-edge roughness, which narrows the Vt and leakage spread (facts 3, 4).

title: Thimble capacitor: ultra-low leakage lets Cs shrink tenfold
idea: Random stimulus 'thimble': a tiny cup is enough if nothing spills. Pair a sub-0.01 fA access device with local short-bitline sense amps so a 0.5 fF stubby capacitor (AR ~8:1) holds the bit, deleting the 60-75:1 pillar etch, the support-mesh wet removal and the many high-AR cleans and IPA/scCO2 dries of today's capacitor module.
why: The capacitor module is one of DRAM's thirstiest loops; a low-AR capacitor cuts its UPW >10x and breaks the charge wall (fact 1) by needing less charge instead of chasing AR 115.

title: Pendulum resonant wordline drivers recycle 3 V swing energy
idea: Random stimulus 'pendulum': energy swings back and forth instead of being thrown away. During refresh bursts, wordlines are driven as part of an LC resonant tank (integrated inductors on the HBM base die), so each 3 V wordline rise and fall returns most of its charge to the tank instead of burning CV^2 through inefficient pumps.
why: Wordline pumps run at ~30-40% efficiency and the 3 V swing is stuck (fact 10); recovering ~80% of wordline energy cuts the wordline share of refresh energy ~10x, and the generation and cooling water embedded in that energy falls by the same factor.

title: Irrigation-ditch water-rights swap funds dry access-module retrofits
idea: Random stimulus 'irrigation ditch': water is a tradable right, not just a pipe. A DRAM fab in a western U.S. water-rights state retrofits its access-device module to dry cleans and area-selective deposition, then leases the freed allocation to farms or cities under a long-term contract; the water utility co-finances the retrofit because it is cheaper than a new supply source.
why: Turns a 10x water cut in the most clean-heavy module into revenue and a permitting advantage, which speeds new U.S. capacity (U.S. manufacturability, capital intensity).

title: Ration-book liters-per-gigabit ceiling for subsidized DRAM fabs
idea: Random stimulus 'ration book': a fixed allotment forces clever cooking. Tie U.S. memory subsidies to a published liters-per-Gb ceiling for the access-device FEOL that steps down 10x over eight years, with bonus credits for adopting dry clean, dry resist, area-selective deposition and product-level refresh-energy cuts.
why: Creates policy pull for a dry access-module toolset (10x water target) and protects fab siting in water-stressed regions, de-risking U.S. DRAM build-out (U.S. manufacturability).

title: Ice-sculpture cryogenic etch leaves no residue to wash
idea: Random stimulus 'ice sculpture': carved cold, and the shavings sublime away. Etch buried-wordline trenches and vertical channels at about -100 C in SF6/O2 or HF-based plasma, where sidewall passivation is a condensed SiOxFy film that sublimes as the wafer warms, so the post-etch polymer wet strip and its rinses disappear.
why: Removes the wet residue-removal loop after each access-module etch (>10x less water there) and gives smoother, less damaged sidewalls with fewer interface traps (fact 3).

title: Vacuum-nanogap field-emission access transistor on sapphire
idea: TRIZ #39 Inert atmosphere (vacuum): a <50 nm vacuum channel, operable near atmospheric pressure because it is shorter than the mean free path of air, separates a sharp emitter from the storage electrode on a sapphire substrate, with a surrounding gate modulating field emission. With no semiconductor in the channel there is no thermal generation or band-to-band leakage in the off state.
why: Off-state leakage effectively zero (Fact 3), radiation-hard and heat-tolerant, so no high-temperature refresh derating; risks are emitter stability and turn-on voltage (Fact 10).

title: Vacuum-channel field-emission nanotriode gates each storage node
idea: Box: stacked cap x lateral ~10 nm vacuum-gap field-emission triode with a hafnium-carbide emitter x current SA x sealed-cavity BEOL tier x Si x self-aligned cavity seal. Below emission threshold the vacuum channel has no band, no generation and no GIDL; a gate pulse thins the barrier for Fowler-Nordheim emission to read/write.
why: Leakage floor set by vacuum, not silicon: retention hours, refresh ~0, and retention becomes temperature-insensitive (fact 3). Emission stability and current density are speculative.

title: Nanoscale vacuum-channel access switch immune to temperature
idea: Worse at 125 C: use any solid channel whose carrier population rises with temperature. Flip: make the access switch a ~20 nm vacuum gap between a sharp field-emission tip and the storage node, gated by the wordline; with a 4.5 eV work function, thermionic current at 125 C is effectively zero.
why: Leakage (fact 3) removed and immune to heat; vacuum does not age over 10 years.

title: Nano-vacuum field-emission access: a vacuum tube shrunk to 10 nm
idea: Scale jump from 1940s vacuum tubes to a sealed ~10 nm cavity: a sharpened Si tip on the storage-node side faces a Si/TiN collector across vacuum, encircled by a gate ring; Fowler-Nordheim emission turns on exponentially only above a gate-field threshold, and below it the gap holds no carriers at all.
why: Access leakage (fact 3) set by tunnelling through vacuum (vanishingly small), so retention is bounded by the dielectric; Si/O/Ti/N only; speculative on emission uniformity and ns-scale current.

title: Vacuum tube returns as nanogap field-emission access transistor
idea: Vacuum tubes and Candescent's field-emission displays died on size, heaters and emitter non-uniformity. Use a ~20 nm vacuum-channel transistor in which a sharp source emits by Fowler-Nordheim tunneling only when the gate lowers the barrier. With no semiconductor in the channel, the off state has no thermal generation and no junction leakage, and a gap shorter than the mean free path does not need hard vacuum.
why: Off-state leakage is set by exponential FN tunneling, so it is effectively zero, and the switch is immune to temperature and radiation. Retention is limited by the capacitor dielectric, so refresh is close to eliminated.

title: Glassblown vacuum-tube nanochannel access switch canned in every cell
idea: Hermetically seal a ~10 nm vacuum gap between a sharpened bitline emitter and a metal storage node, with a surrounding gate electrode, like miniature canned vacuum tubes. Charge moves only by field emission when the gate lowers the barrier.
why: Zero refresh: no semiconductor means no SRH, GIDL or junction leakage, and a junctionless MIM node with thick dielectric leaks <1e-23 A. Retention exceeds years, so refresh is eliminated.

title: Background in-field retention test remaps newly weak rows to spares
idea: Worse at 125 C: trust a factory retention map that ages and drifts over 10 years. Flip: the refresh engine rotates one row per period through an extended-interval check-after-wait test, logs cells that weakened through aging or VRT, and remaps them to spare rows while keeping the rest at relaxed refresh.
why: Keeps relaxed refresh (fact 3) safe for 10 years at 125 C; recovers devices that would fail in the field.

title: Parametron cells: pumped phase-encoded bits that never need refresh
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action: replace static charge with a sustained oscillation. Each cell is a tiny resonator built around a nonlinear (antiferroelectric) varactor, pumped at 2f from a shared plate line; parametric bistability locks it into one of two oscillation phases (0 or pi) that store the bit, and the pump continuously replaces what leakage removes.
why: Eliminates refresh as a concept and makes read non-destructive (Facts 3, 8); risks are resonator size and pump power, reviving Goto's 1954 parametron at nanoscale.

title: Ruthenium redox-molecule storage node holds charge for minutes
idea: Ru: graft a monolayer of Ru-polypyridyl redox molecules on the storage electrode so stored charge lives in discrete molecular oxidation states behind an electron-transfer barrier; the access transistor writes and reads by oxidizing or reducing them, and charge loss needs thermally activated back-transfer (seconds-minutes) rather than ms-scale junction drain.
why: Retention 10^3-10^4x longer cuts refresh energy and bandwidth by the same ratio (fact 3), and redox charge density can exceed a 5 fF pillar's (fact 1).

title: Fermented bacterial S-layer protein crystals as access-pillar etch masks
idea: Ferment bacteria whose surface-layer proteins self-crystallize into 2D lattices with ~10-13 nm period. Harvest and transfer these sheets onto the wafer as hard-mask templates for the vertical access-pillar array.
why: Capital intensity (fact 4): replaces 1-2 EUV or multi-patterning steps with a bioreactor. Atomically identical protein pores tighten pillar diameter, so VT and leakage spread narrow and the tail shrinks.

title: Burrowing mole's shortcut: heterojunction tunnel-FET access at 0.5 V
idea: A mole tunnels through the hill instead of climbing it. The access device is a vertical Ge-source/Si-channel tunnel FET: band-to-band tunneling turns it on within ~0.3 V at sub-60 mV/dec, and when off the tunneling window closes, leaving no thermionic tail.
why: A ~0.5 V wordline instead of a pumped 3 V cuts wordline energy ~30x; the low on-current is acceptable on short local bitlines, giving >=10x lower access energy.

title: Banker's insured deposits: refresh-free banks for data with backups
idea: A banker guards insured deposits lightly because losses are covered. Pages with a valid copy elsewhere (model weights, page cache, read-only datasets) go into banks run with refresh off or at 1-4 s, protected by strong per-line detection codes; a detected error triggers a transparent refetch from flash, CXL or a remote replica instead of a crash.
why: Read-mostly AI weights are a large share of DRAM; dropping their refresh cuts refresh power and bandwidth 50-90% in those banks with only detection metadata added.

title: Kiln-shrunk silicon dots make a Coulomb-blockade multi-junction access chain
idea: Like clay shrinking in a kiln, use self-limiting oxidation to shrink Si islands to ~1.5 nm, forming a chain of 4-6 tunnel junctions between bitline and storage node. The chain's Coulomb blockade is lifted only when the side gate is pulsed.
why: Zero refresh: cotunneling leakage falls exponentially with junction count, giving retention of days to years at room temperature with no semiconductor junction to leak.

title: Constant-bias field plate over storage junction suppresses GIDL
idea: Po: the drain sees no electric field. Split the buried wordline into an active gate over the channel and a separate field-plate segment over the storage-node overlap held at a fixed mild positive bias, so the gate-to-drain field that drives band-to-band GIDL never forms even while the active gate sits at negative hold.
why: Fact 3: GIDL is a main tail mechanism under negative wordline; removing it allows deeper negative hold and 3-5x lower tail leakage.

title: Molybdenum-gate MOS revived: graded-work-function wordlines that cut GIDL
idea: Revive the refractory molybdenum-gate MOSFETs of the 1970s: replace tungsten buried wordlines with Colorado-mined molybdenum whose nitrogen content is graded with depth, so the gate work function is high over the channel (good Vt) and low where the gate overlaps the drain (less band bending), suppressing GIDL.
why: GIDL is a dominant tail mechanism (fact 3), targeted at ~10x lower; also removes dependence on China's ~80% share of tungsten.

title: Parametric phase bits in high-Q nanomechanical resonators
idea: Po: the bit is a rhythm, not a charge. Revive Goto's parametron: each cell is a nanomechanical resonator pumped at twice its natural frequency, which settles into oscillation at phase 0 or pi; the phase is the bit, held while the shared pump runs, written by a seed pulse and read by a phase detector.
why: Facts 1 and 3: no capacitor and no leakage decay; the shared pump replaces refresh; speculative on density and pump power per bit.

title: Goto's parametron stores bits as phase in NEMS resonators
idea: The parametron, which stored bits as the oscillation phase of parametrically pumped resonators, lost to transistors on speed. Store each bit as the 0 or pi phase of a high-Q nanomechanical resonator pumped at 2f from a shared line, and read it by phase-sensitive detection. There is no leakage to fight, only pump power of roughly stored energy times omega/Q.
why: Refresh is replaced by continuous pump power, estimated at ~0.5 pW/bit for Q~1e4. That is comparable to today's refresh power but has no access-transistor tail, so retention rests on different physics. Density is speculative.

title: Plumbing check-valve pair: ultra-high-barrier Schottky diodes guard the node
idea: Isolate each metal storage node with two back-to-back high-barrier Schottky rectifiers (e.g., Pt/Ga2O3, ~1.8 eV) to separate write-high and write-low lines, like check valves cast into a pipe tee. Pulsing the line past the barrier fills or drains the node.
why: Zero refresh: thermionic reverse leakage over a 1.8 eV barrier is ~1e-30 A per cell, so retention exceeds the product's life. A two-terminal access device also removes the transistor and simplifies the wordline.

title: Panel-scale DRAM made on display oxide-TFT glass lines
idea: IFR: memory as cheap per square meter as a television. Use Gen 8.5+ display fabs' oxide-TFT lines (1-1.5 um features, ultralow-leak IGZO-class TFTs already in mass production) to build huge-area 1T1C tiles, with CMOS sense and I/O chiplets bonded along tile edges so each panel holds hundreds of GB.
why: Capital and US manufacturability: display processing costs ~$100-300/m^2, orders of magnitude below wafer $/area, and refresh-light oxide TFTs make a cheap capacity tier without wafer fabs.

title: Regulatory idle-watts-per-terabyte metric forcing refresh-aware servers
idea: Po: refresh is illegal. Add a measured idle-memory-watts-per-TB line to server efficiency rules and large procurement specs (ENERGY STAR, EU ecodesign, federal data-center buys), tested in self-refresh, so vendors must ship temperature-compensated refresh, partial-array self-refresh and OS free-page hints enabled by default.
why: Fact 3: refresh is 16-33% of idle DRAM power; scoring it pushes features already in silicon into deployment, cutting fleet refresh energy 2-4x.

title: Rent a furnace: high-pressure deuterium anneal of purchased DRAM wafers
idea: 10-person constraint: one tool, no fab. Buy known-good DRAM wafers before dicing and run a high-pressure (10-20 atm) deuterium anneal at 350-400 C, which drives D through the BEOL stack to passivate residual Si/SiO2 dangling bonds at the access transistors. Re-sort the results into long-retention bins and sell them as low-refresh parts.
why: Fact 3: high-pressure anneal studies show large interface-trap reductions, which could compress the leakage tail ~2-5x. A 10-person shop with one HP anneal tool creates a premium grade. Risk: BEOL thermal budget.

title: Resonant LC bitline drive recycles refresh energy adiabatically
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x SA swung by a resonant LC tank x in-package spiral inductors per bank x Si x standard. During refresh bursts bitline groups swing through the tank so charge oscillates between groups and inductor instead of being dumped to ground, recovering ~60-80% of CV2.
why: Refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit, fact 3) cut 2-4x; same circuit can serve normal activations.

title: Junctionless gate-all-around access continuous with the storage electrode
idea: Channel and storage node are one uniformly n+ doped nanowire, turned off by full depletion from a gate-all-around wordline. There is no metallurgical pn junction at the storage node.
why: Removes junction leakage and the abrupt-junction GIDL hotspot, which may give a 10-100x lower tail at sub-10 nm wire diameters.

title: Room-temperature Coulomb-blockade island isolates the storage node
idea: Scale jump to the few-nanometre quantum dot: insert a sub-2 nm silicon nanocrystal between access channel and storage node so the single-electron charging energy (~200-300 meV) exceeds 8 kT; in hold the bias sits inside the blockade window so leakage is exponentially suppressed, while the wordline shifts the dot level to allow ns sequential tunnelling during access.
why: Access leakage tail (fact 3): blockade adds 4-6 decades of off-state suppression independent of transistor Vt, potentially minutes of retention.

title: AlGaN/GaN polarization well storing floating 2DEG charge for days
idea: Po: the electron is locked in a polarization cage. Use a floating AlGaN/GaN island as the gate of a read transistor; the polarization-induced 2DEG well in 3.4 eV GaN holds electrons with negligible thermal generation for days, written through a thin AlN tunnel barrier.
why: Facts 1 and 3 plus U.S. manufacturability (GaN-on-Si lines exist domestically): quasi-nonvolatile capacitorless storage cuts refresh ~1000x.

title: Recompute instead of refresh: checksummed recomputable activations
idea: 10-person constraint: a software library. Mark tensors that are cheap to recompute (activations saved for the backward pass, KV-cache prefixes) as recompute-on-loss and store them in relaxed-refresh regions (e.g. 1 s), with a 32-bit checksum per tile. On a mismatch, recompute the tile from its checkpointed inputs instead of paying refresh to protect it.
why: Fact 3: trades rare recomputation (<0.1% of FLOPs) for near-zero refresh on a large share of training memory.

title: Minify dark carriers: light-gated photoconductive access switches
idea: Use a wide-bandgap photoconductor strip (amorphous GaN or ZnS, dark resistivity >1e14 ohm-cm) as each access switch, turned on by an on-chip waveguide routing 365 nm light to the selected row through micro-ring selectors; in the dark it is an insulator and there is no wordline to charge.
why: Leakage ~0 in the dark; eliminates 3 V wordline CV^2 (fact 10); refresh far rarer; switching speed and optical power budget are the risks.

title: Light-gated access: optical wordlines and dark-off photoconductive switches
idea: Scale jump from fibre optics to the cell: replace the electrically gated access transistor with a wide-bandgap photoconductive bridge (e.g., SiC or diamond-like carbon film) addressed by on-chip waveguide wordlines; in the dark the bridge is an insulator with no thermal carriers across ~3 eV, and a ~100 ps blue/UV pulse along the waveguide row makes it conduct for read or write.
why: Leakage/refresh (fact 3) and the 3 V wordline (fact 10): no gate voltage at all and dark leakage set by bandgap, potentially seconds-to-hours retention.

title: Eliminate plasma-etch damage: KOH crystallographic (111) sidewall vertical channel
idea: Define vertical access-transistor channels by anisotropic KOH/TMAH etching of (110) silicon so channel sidewalls are atomically flat (111) planes instead of plasma-roughened surfaces, then grow thermal gate oxide. Lower interface-state density and no etch damage remove generation and VRT centers.
why: Interface traps drive trap-assisted tunneling and variable retention; 5-10x lower Dit narrows the retention tail (fact 3) with cheap wet etching.

title: Thresholds must move only twice per idle: ferroelectric Vt-parking access transistor
idea: Limit: leakage may be killed only by a stored state, not by continuous bias. Embed a thin HZO layer in the access gate stack. Before a long idle, one global pulse polarizes it so every access transistor's Vt rises ~0.5 V ('parked', ~1e8 lower subthreshold leakage); an un-park pulse restores the low Vt before access. Ferroelectric endurance is spent only on rare idle transitions.
why: Fact 3: self-refresh dominates idle power. Parked arrays could hold data for minutes between refreshes, a 100x+ cut in standby refresh energy. This is distinct from using HZO as the storage element.

title: Run memory at 150-200 K and redesign the access device for it
idea: TRIZ #35 Parameter change: change temperature instead of geometry. Cooling DRAM to ~150-200 K on a shared refrigerant loop cuts thermal leakage by many orders so retention reaches minutes; then exploit it by lowering the access-transistor Vt and shortening its channel for a smaller, faster cell at lower wordline voltage.
why: Refresh practically disappears (Fact 3) and lower Vt enables lower VPP (Fact 10): claim >50% memory energy reduction net of cooling at rack scale.

title: Cold-source access FET filters the thermal electron tail
idea: Worse: accept the 60 mV/dec Boltzmann tail that sets off-current. Flip: build the bitline-side source as an n+/p+ superlattice whose density of states is cut off above the band edge, so only cold electrons inject and the slope reaches ~35-40 mV/dec.
why: Off-current about 1000x lower at the same Vt and wordline swing; attacks leakage (fact 3) and allows lower VPP (fact 10).

title: Minify the swing with a band-to-band tunneling access FET
idea: Make the access device a vertical heterojunction TFET (SiGe source at the bitline, Si channel, drain into storage node) whose off-state has no thermionic Boltzmann tail, so off-current is set by tunneling (~1e-18 A). Its low on-current is offset by short local bitlines.
why: Off-current decoupled from kT: refresh interval ~10x longer, and wordline swing can fall from ~3 V to ~1.5 V (fact 10).

title: USDA-style retention grade stamp and JEDEC refresh-optional mode
idea: Like USDA grading stamps on meat and eggs, require every DRAM die to carry a tested retention grade (e.g., R1 >= 250 ms, R2 >= 2 s at 85 C) and standardize a JEDEC mode that disables refresh per bank. Software can then target refresh-free placement.
why: Zero refresh power deployable at scale: makes refresh-disabled operation a standard, verifiable product attribute instead of a lab trick.

title: Qualify DRAM cold: a liquid-cooled retention grade
idea: Rearrange the spec around the deployment: create a datasheet grade qualified at <=55 C case temperature for direct-liquid-cooled racks, where retention is ~8x longer than at 85 C. Dies that fail 85 C retention screening but pass at 55 C enter this grade instead of downgrade or scrap, and all parts in the grade run 2-4x slower refresh.
why: Raises usable supply from existing fab output by recovering retention fallout and cuts refresh energy (fact 3); a test-flow and spec change only.

title: Ski patrol's avalanche trigger: feedback-FET access switch
idea: Ski patrol releases a whole avalanche with one small charge. The access device is a gated p-i-n-i-n feedback FET whose intrinsic regions are electrostatically doped by the gate; past threshold, injected carriers collapse the internal barriers by positive feedback, giving <1 mV/dec switching at ~0.5 V and a hard barrier when off.
why: A ~0.5 V wordline instead of 3 V cuts wordline CV^2 ~36x with very high on/off, putting total access energy >=10x lower; hysteresis must be tuned so the device releases cleanly.

title: Thinfilm's yield problem solved by self-clearing printed electrodes
idea: Thinfilm's printed memories struggled with yield because of pinholes and leaky spots. Borrow the self-healing of metallized-film capacitors: print 20 nm aluminium top electrodes, so that during a burn-in pulse any leakage hot spot heats up and vaporizes the electrode around it. That disconnects the leaky cell, which is then mapped out instead of setting the retention time.
why: Physically clips the leakage tail of printed arrays, so refresh is set by intrinsic leakage rather than defects. Printable.

title: High-pressure deuterium anneal hardens traps behind the leakage tail
idea: Effect: kinetic isotope effect. Replace the final forming-gas anneal with 10-20 atm D2 so Si-D bonds passivate interface and GIDL-region traps; Si-D resists field- and hot-carrier-driven depassivation ~10-50x better than Si-H, so fewer traps reactivate into weak or VRT cells over life. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): ~2x longer guaranteed internal refresh period; deuterium from heavy water is not a chokepoint.

title: Eliminate thermal generation: 4H-SiC MOS dynamic memory cell
idea: Build 1T1C cells on purchased 4H-SiC epi wafers with NO-annealed thermal oxide and an npn or MOS access device; with a 3.26 eV gap the thermal generation rate is ~1e-17 of silicon's, so stored charge lasts hours or longer at room temperature, as early academic SiC test cells showed. University fabs already process SiC power devices.
why: Refresh essentially eliminated (fact 3) and cells tolerate hot packages; U.S. SiC wafer supply exists; density and cost per bit are the challenge.

title: Vacuum-tube getter revived inside sealed BEOL cavities
idea: Revive the barium flash getter that kept vacuum tubes clean for decades: deposit a non-evaporable Zr-V-Fe getter film in a sealed cavity over each array mat, activated by the final anneal. It keeps absorbing the hydrogen and moisture that would otherwise migrate to access-transistor interfaces over life, creating trap-assisted leakage and variable retention time.
why: Keeps the tail stable (fact 3) over a 10-year life, so the ~2x refresh guardband can shrink; targets a 1.5-2x longer refresh interval and fewer VRT failures.

title: PLEDM resurrected with one epitaxial CaF2 tunnel barrier
idea: Hitachi's PLEDM vertical gain cell used a stack of Si3N4/poly-Si tunnel barriers, which made writes slow and the process complex. Replace the stack with one ~1.5 nm CaF2 barrier, grown epitaxially and lattice-matched on Si under the storage node. A surrounding gate bends the Si bands to open tunneling for writes. Because the barrier is a trap-free crystal, the off-state has no trap-assisted tunneling tail.
why: A vertical 4F2 gain cell with no capacitor, whose leakage tail is set by a crystalline barrier with no SRH or trap tail. Claimed retention is seconds, refresh is ~100x rarer, and the cell can be stacked.

title: Eliminate thermionic injection: Ge/Si heterojunction tunnel FET access device
idea: Build a vertical tunnel FET with a CVD-grown p+ Ge source on an n-type Si channel so carriers enter only by band-to-band tunneling; at hold bias the tunneling window closes and there is no thermionic tail, giving ~1e-18 A/um off current. The low on current is fine because one cell needs only microamps.
why: Leakage 100-1000x below MOSFET access devices at equal gate bias, enabling ~10x longer refresh intervals; university CVD plus RTA.

title: Eliminate leakage pathways: Coulomb-blockade-locked silicon nanodot storage node
idea: Store a small charge on a 2-3 nm Si nanodot (LPCVD-grown or e-beam defined) that gates a sense FET and is separated from the bitline by a tunnel barrier; the >100 meV Coulomb charging energy blocks single-electron escape at hold bias, exponentially suppressing leakage. A write gate lowers the barrier.
why: Retention could exceed seconds with non-destructive gain-transistor reads (facts 3, 8); room-temperature blockade needs sub-3 nm uniformity.

title: Silicon NEMS relay as access switch: an air gap never leaks
idea: Scale jump from the telephone relay to a 60 nm silicon beam: each cell's access device is a doubly clamped Si beam pulled onto a TiN contact by the wordline's electrostatic force; when released, a ~5 nm gap gives effectively zero off-current, so retention is limited only by the capacitor dielectric.
why: Leakage/refresh (fact 3): channel leakage vanishes and refresh intervals stretch to seconds-minutes; switching ~1-5 ns at this scale; the risk is stiction and >1e15-cycle contact endurance; materials Si, Ti, N only.

title: Eliminate lithography: block-copolymer self-assembled pillars for vertical access transistors
idea: Spin a PS-b-PMMA block copolymer, anneal it into a hexagonal 20-30 nm pitch pattern, transfer it into silicon as vertical pillars, and build surrounding-gate access transistors whose channel length is set by etch depth (long, low-leakage), not lithography. Only contact lithography is used for coarse alignment.
why: Removes EUV from the access-device level (fact 4) and allows long vertical channels in a 4F^2 footprint, lowering leakage; registration and defectivity are the risk.

title: Allocator-driven REFSKIP command cancels refresh of dead data
idea: Worse: keep refreshing memory nobody will read again. Flip: add a DDR/CXL REFSKIP range command that the allocator, garbage collector and KV-cache evictor issue on free; the DRAM clears a per-row live bit and its refresh engine skips dead rows until the next write.
why: Refresh energy (fact 3) down in proportion to free memory, typically 20-50% on servers.

title: Sperry MNOS shadow trap: access transistor stores a sleep copy
idea: Revive Sperry's 1967 metal-nitride-oxide-semiconductor memory: give the access transistor a thin nitride charge-trap layer. On entering deep sleep, a row-by-row pulse injects trap charge according to each cell's bit (1e5-1e6 cycles is ample for sleep events) and the array powers off with zero refresh; on wake, the trap-shifted Vt is sensed and rewritten to the capacitor.
why: Removes self-refresh power, 16-33% of idle (fact 3), for idle servers and phones: zero retention power during sleep.

title: Minify write voltage to 100 mV: magnetoelectric BiFeO3-gated nanomagnets
idea: Couple a multiferroic BiFeO3 layer to a CoFe nanomagnet so a ~100 mV field reverses BFO polarization and, via exchange coupling, flips the magnet; an MTJ stacked on top reads it. Write current is capacitive only, so the access transistor can be minimum-width.
why: Non-volatile, aJ-class write, escapes the CV^2 voltage floor (fact 10); FE endurance in BFO is the limit.

title: Legacy-node always-on island lets modern DRAM fully power down
idea: Put a 32-64 MB refresh-free die on the package (180 nm thick-oxide or loadless cells) holding page tables, kernel and wake state. Modern DRAM banks then enter deep power-down with no refresh when idle, flushing or discarding their contents.
why: Idle refresh power (16-33%) goes to near zero for phones and lightly loaded servers, and U.S. legacy fabs make the island.

title: Core memory's hand-threading killed it; print planar ferrite cores
idea: Ferrite core memory died because the cores had to be threaded by hand. Print soft-ferrite nanoparticle rings in planar form on a web, with screen-printed silver X, Y and sense windings, and read them by coincident-current half-select. There is no access transistor, so there is no leakage and no refresh.
why: A transistor-free, refresh-free, radiation-hard working-memory tier made roll-to-roll from abundant iron oxide. Density is low (~1 Mb/cm2), so the targets are edge and defense uses and supply diversity.

title: Xerographic amorphous-selenium photoconductor as optically gated access switch
idea: Revive xerography's amorphous-selenium photoreceptor (dark resistivity ~1e14-1e15 ohm-cm) and the vidicon target: each cell's access element is a tiny a-Se photoconductor between bitline and capacitor, gated by light from silicon-nitride waveguide wordlines. Selenium is refined in Utah and the waveguides come from U.S. photonics foundries.
why: Dark off-state leakage sits far below MOS subthreshold (fact 3), and optical wordlines remove wordline-to-cell electrical coupling (fact 9) and the 3 V wordline swing (fact 10). Photoconductor response time limits speed.

title: Esaki-diode bistable cells restored by one global plate pulse
idea: Worse: refresh by activating 8 KB rows one at a time through sense amps. Flip: add a vertical tunnel-diode pair on each storage node to create an NDR latch with two stable voltages, then periodically pulse the shared cell plate so every cell in a mat snaps back to its own stable point at once, with no sensing or row activation.
why: Removes the 10-20% refresh bandwidth loss and most of the ~46 fJ/bit refresh energy (fact 3).

title: Co-decaying reference cells enable 16-level DRAM storage
idea: IFR: decay does not matter if the ruler shrinks with the data. Each row carries 15 reference cells written at the level boundaries together with the data; they leak through identical access devices at identical temperature, so a ramp-ADC sense amp compares against references that drift exactly as the data does, allowing 4 bits per gain cell.
why: Constraint: 4x bits for a few percent array area and no added masks; combined with three cheap deposition tiers or a 4F^2 vertical cell it reaches ~10x bits at near-equal wafer cost.

title: Minify the switch to two terminals: OTS selector plus FE capacitor
idea: Pair each ferroelectric capacitor with an ovonic threshold switch selector in a 1S1C stack: half-select voltages stay below the OTS threshold so unselected cells see no disturb, while the selected cell gets the full switching pulse; 4-8 layers stack above CMOS periphery.
why: Eliminates planar access transistor area and epitaxial silicon per layer; non-volatile 3D density multiplication.

title: High-pressure deuterium anneal hardens interfaces against the leakage tail
idea: Replace the final forming-gas anneal with a high-pressure deuterium furnace anneal, a 1990s hot-carrier fix. Si-D bonds resist breaking far better than Si-H, so fewer interface traps form to drive trap-assisted GIDL and VRT.
why: Shrinks the VRT and tail population 2-5x, allowing a 2x longer refresh interval for one cheap furnace step.

title: Self-limiting oxidation sharpens DUV pillars into sub-10 nm access channels
idea: O: pattern ~40 nm silicon pillars with DUV and thermally oxidize them; compressive stress in curved oxide retards oxidation as the core shrinks, so it self-terminates at a nearly uniform ~8-10 nm core regardless of starting CD, which becomes a gate-all-around vertical access channel after oxide strip.
why: Converts DUV CD variation into a self-limiting physical endpoint, giving thin uniform channels (low leakage, tight Vt) below EUV dimensions without EUV (facts 3, 4).

title: Magnetically latched FeCo nanorelay gives true open-circuit access
idea: Fe: replace the access transistor with a vertical FeCo nanocantilever relay with Ru contacts, pulled closed electrostatically by the wordline and biased by a CoPt permanent-magnet film so it latches open or closed; the off state is a vacuum gap with zero subthreshold or junction leakage.
why: Retention becomes limited only by capacitor dielectric leakage (hours), removing refresh (fact 3); contact wear (~10^15 cycles needed) is the risk, so pair it with an SRAM/cache layer that limits per-cell switching.

title: Self-cleaning oven: wordline Joule heating anneals away the leakage tail
idea: Adapted from pyrolytic self-cleaning ovens and Macronix's self-healing NAND: during maintenance windows, drive a controlled current through selected buried wordlines to heat local cells to ~250-400 C for milliseconds, annealing traps and re-passivating interfaces that hot-carrier and hammer stress created over the module's life.
why: Repairable in place: rather than guard-banding refresh for end-of-life growth of the leakage tail (fact 3), the tail is periodically reset, extending service life and keeping refresh margins tight.

title: FeFET depolarization failure becomes hours-long dynamic retention
idea: FeFETs, from Bell Labs to modern devices, failed as nonvolatile memory because the depolarization field and charge trapping erased their state within days. Store the bit instead in an antiferroelectric ZrO2 capacitor whose field-induced polar state is weakly stabilized by electrodes with mismatched work functions (built-in imprint). The state decays over hours rather than milliseconds, and it is read nondestructively through its field-dependent capacitance.
why: A 'slow-leak DRAM' that refreshes every few hours instead of every 32-64 ms, ~1e5x fewer refreshes. The cell never fully switches polarization, so it avoids fatigue.

title: Silicon-on-nothing pocket removes the storage-node junction's bottom area
idea: Si: use an empty-space-in-silicon process (etch a hole array, hydrogen-anneal so silicon migrates and seals a void) to place a vacuum pocket beneath each storage-node diffusion, leaving the junction floating with only its sidewall touching the body.
why: Junction generation leakage scales with depleted area/volume (fact 3); deleting the bottom face cuts that component ~2-5x and stops substrate minority-carrier collection that disturbs neighbor cells.

title: Pinch-valve access: piezo-squeezed channel that physically closes the conduction path
idea: Pinch valves seal by squeezing a tube flat instead of holding back pressure. Build the access element from a piezoresistive Mott material (SmSe-type) clamped by a thin relaxor piezoelectric driven by the wordline: strained, the material goes metallic; unstrained, it is a wide-gap insulator, so there is no gate-controlled subthreshold tail at all.
why: Replaces exponential subthreshold behavior with a pressure-driven insulator-metal transition switching at ~0.1-0.3 V, attacking both the voltage floor (fact 10) and leakage (fact 3).

title: Wordline hot-wire annealing heals retention in the field
idea: Periodically drive a calibrated current pulse through a wordline segment, as hot-wire annealing or blade tempering does, to flash-heat the gate stack to ~300-400 C for microseconds. The pulse re-passivates interface traps and resets VRT defects that grew during service.
why: Retention degradation over life and VRT: restoring the tail ~2x late in life avoids derating refresh rates and extends module service life.

title: 1952 Bell licensing redux: open-license a low-leakage access cell
idea: Revive Bell Labs' 1952 transistor licensing symposium, which sold patent rights cheaply to any firm and seeded an industry: a national lab or consortium develops a refresh-relaxed access-device module and licenses it, with a process design kit and test structures, to every U.S. fab for a nominal fee.
why: Multiplies domestic low-refresh memory capacity (fact 3, U.S. manufacturability) and cuts each fab's R&D bill and time to market.

title: Neutron transmutation doping at U.S. research reactors for implant-free channels
idea: Revive 1970s neutron transmutation doping, used for power-device silicon: irradiate silicon at U.S. research reactors (for example the University of Missouri reactor) so Si-30 transmutes into uniformly distributed phosphorus. Access-transistor wells then form without implantation, removing the implant-damage clusters that seed trap-assisted leakage.
why: The extreme tail cells come largely from implant-damage defects (fact 3); implant-free, uniform wells could cut tail cells per die several-fold and allow longer refresh.

title: Tail-bit eviction table lets the bulk array refresh 16x slower
idea: TRIZ #2 Taking out: extract the few harmful cells instead of running the whole array at their pace. At final test each die is screened against a 1 s / 85 C retention target; the ~1e-5 of bits that fail are fuse-mapped into a per-bank CAM + SRAM 'tail cache' (~32 kb) that transparently intercepts their reads and writes, with on-die ECC covering variable-retention escapees.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth (Fact 3): refresh is set by the 99.999th percentile, not the worst cell, giving 8-16x fewer refresh operations for ~0.3-0.5% die area; idle refresh power drops from 16-33% to a few percent.

title: Airgap between buried wordlines kills passing-gate leakage
idea: Scale shift from BEOL low-k airgaps down to the buried-wordline level: after wordline recess, ash out a sacrificial carbon liner between adjacent wordline trenches to leave sealed airgaps (k=1), so an active neighbour wordline no longer capacitively lifts the access channel or injects carriers into adjacent storage nodes.
why: Passing-gate leakage and hammer-induced charge loss (facts 3, 9): ~2-3x lower coupling means fewer prematurely decaying cells and less refresh and mitigation overhead, using C and O2 only.

title: Substitute helium cryogenics with liquid-nitrogen-immersed DRAM tier
idea: Substitute any helium cryostat with 77 K liquid-nitrogen immersion for a pooled-memory sled; the nitrogen comes from air separation, with no helium or neon. At 77 K subthreshold and junction leakage fall more than 1e6x and retention reaches hours, so the access transistor can use a lower Vt and a ~1.5 V wordline.
why: Refresh essentially disappears, wordline energy drops ~4x and wire resistance ~5x; cryocooler energy is traded for density and refresh savings in a disaggregated pool.

title: Accordion-folded single membrane becomes 26 tiers of crystalline cells
idea: Process one planar single-crystal membrane (SOI device layer) with lateral access transistors in a strip pattern, release it, then fold it accordion-style like a road map using prestressed hinge lines. N folds yield N tiers that all came from one high-quality planar process.
why: Fact 2: gives 3D DRAM single-crystal lateral transistors for every tier while using only planar processing once. Folding replaces 26x deposition/etch loops.

title: Photosynthetic self-refresh cells restored by a global light pulse
idea: Leaves turn light into stored energy without wires; put a tiny photodiode under each storage node, tied to VARY through a restore transistor gated by the storage node itself, so a periodic chip-wide backside flash at ~1.1 um tops up only cells holding '1' while '0' cells' restore path stays off.
why: Refresh needs no row activation, bitline swing or command slots, so the 10-20% bandwidth loss goes to ~0 and refresh energy can fall >5x if photo-efficiency and light isolation hold.

title: Calcium-transient diffusive selector as a volatile two-terminal access switch
idea: Synaptic Ca2+ floods in and is cleared within ms; use an Ag-nanocluster diffusive threshold switch in sputtered SiO2 (room temperature) as the access device: a bitline-wordline pulse forms a filament that spontaneously dissolves within ~1 us, leaving a high-resistance off-state with ~1e10 on/off.
why: Two-terminal access lets 4F2 crosspoint DRAM tiers stack in BEOL without a transistor or EUV gate layers; the open problems are fA-level off-current and 1e15 endurance.

title: Threshold-switch crossbar capacitors: 64 decks, refreshed constantly
idea: Inverts 'an access device must hold the bit for 64 ms': put a chalcogenide ovonic threshold switch in series with a tiny MIM capacitor at every crossbar node, stack 64 self-aligned decks with two KrF masks each, accept us-to-ms retention set by OTS leakage, and refresh whole decks in parallel from base CMOS.
why: 4F2 per deck with no transistor or EUV, ~100x cheaper per GB; trade-off is refresh power (~20-40% of total), half-select disturb and OTS drift.

title: Self-dissolving silver filament as two-terminal crosspoint access element
idea: A diffusive Ag:SiO2 threshold switch grows a sub-nm Ag bridge above ~0.4 V. When bias drops, surface energy breaks the bridge up within ~100 ns, leaving a 2-5 nm insulating gap (ON/OFF ~1e9-1e10, slope <1 mV/dec). Put one in series with each capacitor in a 4F^2 1S1C crosspoint biased so half-selected cells never cross threshold.
why: The access device becomes a gap-limited switch with near-ideal steepness. It removes the transistor footprint (6F^2 to 4F^2) and junction leakage (fact 3). The core risk is endurance: ~1e10 cycles is demonstrated, and 1e15 or more is needed.

title: Selenide threshold switch builds a crosspoint one-selector-one-capacitor DRAM
idea: Se: replace the three-terminal access transistor with a two-terminal Ge-As-Se ovonic threshold switch stacked on a vertical capacitor at 4F2 crosspoint pitch; selected cells see V above threshold (~1.5 V), half-selected cells see V/2, and Se-rich, N-doped compositions push sub-threshold leakage toward the fA regime.
why: 4F2 density and stackable decks without a lateral transistor (facts 2, 4); viability needs OTS off-current ~10^3 below today's, so physics risk is honestly high.

title: SSD pSLC trick: aging regions downgrade to twin-cell differential mode
idea: Adapted from SSDs that run worn TLC blocks in pseudo-SLC mode: when telemetry shows a region's retention degrading, the controller reformats it so each bit uses two adjacent cells storing complementary charge, sensed differentially. The region loses half its capacity but gains ~4x retention and stays in service.
why: Graceful degradation instead of replacement: aging access devices (fact 3) no longer force faster refresh chip-wide or scrapping; capacity sheds in small steps and module life extends by years.

title: LCD panel laser repair: hydrogen-ambient spot anneal heals mapped tail cells
idea: Display fabs laser-repair defective pixels after test instead of scrapping panels. After retention mapping at wafer sort, scan a focused infrared laser through the thinned wafer backside in D2/H2 ambient over regions holding tail cells, briefly heating buried interfaces to re-passivate traps; only photons and hydrogen, no fluorine.
why: Repairs the few-ppm tail locally without adding thermal budget to the whole wafer, turning refresh-limiting cells normal (fact 3) and recovering retention-limited yield.

title: Intel-Opticom polymer ferroelectric becomes a zero-refresh sleep shadow
idea: Intel and Opticom's printed P(VDF-TrFE) polymer memory failed as main memory because of microsecond switching, fatigue and disturb. Print it instead as a per-row shadow layer over an oxide-TFT memory foil. When the foil enters sleep, each row copies itself into its polymer shadow (slow, rare writes), and power and refresh drop to zero. On wake, the rows restore.
why: Eliminates refresh energy during idle. Fatigue stops mattering at ~1e4 sleep cycles over a lifetime, and the shadow is an additive printed layer.

title: Timing knobs only: extended restore time for weak rows
idea: 10-person constraint: only controller timing registers. Weak rows often fail because tight tRAS/tWR truncates their restore and leaves them at ~85-90% charge. The controller flags weak rows from profiling and gives only those activations and writes an extra 5-10 ns of restore, so the cell charges fully and its retention clears the slow-refresh threshold.
why: Fact 3: 10-20% more stored charge raises weak-row retention ~1.5-2x, which lets the global refresh tier relax a notch at under 0.1% performance cost.

title: Resonant-tunneling access diode opens only at wordline-tuned resonance
idea: Effect: double-barrier resonant tunneling. Replace the access transistor with a vertical AlN/GaN/AlN (or SiO2/Si-well/SiO2) stack whose quantized well level aligns with the storage-node Fermi level only when the wordline, acting as a gate on the well, pulls it into resonance; off-resonance transmission is 10^6-10^9 lower and fixed by barrier thickness rather than doping.
why: 3D blocker (fact 2): a thin vertical film stack replaces the lateral transistor, so tiers stack without lithography of channels; leakage decoupled from channel length (fact 4).

title: Squeeze to switch: strain-gated piezoelectronic access device
idea: Inverts 'a switch is gated by a field in its channel': an AlScN or PMN-PT piezo actuator compresses a SmSe-type piezoresistive channel that undergoes a pressure-driven insulator-to-metal transition; uncompressed, the channel is a true gapped insulator with no subthreshold tail, and actuation needs <0.2 V.
why: Isolation without a subthreshold tail (fact 3) and sub-volt wordlines (fact 10), cutting wordline CV2 ~10x and refresh to near zero.

title: Wordlines capped at VARY: negative-capacitance HZO gate amplifies switching
idea: Limit: no wordline may exceed the array voltage. Add a 5 nm Zr-rich HZO negative-capacitance layer to the access transistor gate stack, capacitance-matched to the channel so internal voltage amplification gives ~40 mV/dec hysteresis-free switching. The same Ion/Ioff then needs ~1 V less swing, or the same swing gives ~25x lower leakage.
why: Facts 3, 7 and 10: retires the boosted 3 V wordline and its charge pumps (periphery area), or lengthens retention ~10x. Unlike prior HZO memory work, the ferroelectric is a gain element inside the switch, not the storage.

title: Turn GIDL into the switch: band-to-band tunnel-FET access device
idea: Reverse the role of the worst leakage mechanism: GIDL is band-to-band tunneling at the gate edge, so make that the ON mechanism with a p-i-n tunnel-FET access device (SiGe/Ge source pocket at the bitline end). The off state has no thermionic path, giving aA-level off current and sub-60 mV/dec swing, and DRAM tolerates the TFET's low on-current because a 5 fF cell needs only ~1-5 uA to write in a few ns.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): off current 100-1000x below the ~13 fA tail could stretch retention from 64 ms to seconds; the smaller wordline swing also eases the voltage floor (fact 10).

title: Gated Esaki-diode latch makes each cell self-holding
idea: IFR: the bit stays put with no refresh and no extra transistors. Engineer the storage-node junction as a degenerate band-to-band tunnel diode in series with a gated load so the node has two stable points on an N-shaped I-V (Goto-pair style), held by a picoamp-scale standby current.
why: Fact 3: refresh disappears; at ~1 pA x 1 V per cell a Gb-class die idles at ~10 mW, competitive with refresh, with quantum-well tunnel diodes targeting 10 fA holding current.

title: Domestic heavy water revived for deuterium-passivated access transistors
idea: Revive the U.S. heavy-water production of the 1950s to supply domestic deuterium for high-pressure D2 anneals of access transistors and buried-wordline interfaces. Si-D bonds resist hot-carrier and wordline-stress depassivation far better than Si-H, so the interface traps behind GIDL and variable retention stay passivated over life.
why: Stabilizes the leakage tail and VRT (fact 3), letting refresh guardbands shrink 1.5-2x, with a secure domestic D2 supply.

title: Substitute argon-purged Cz crystal with hydrogen-ambient crucible-free silicon
idea: Substitute argon-purged Czochralski pulling in quartz crucibles with electromagnetic cold-crucible casting in a hydrogen/nitrogen ambient for the substrate. The access transistors live in a 3-5 um low-oxygen epitaxial layer grown by H2-carrier CVD, with nitrogen co-doping for gettering.
why: Removes the argon and Spruce Pine quartz chokepoints, and low-oxygen epi has fewer generation centers, so the leakage tail improves rather than worsens.

title: Detector-grade crucible-free float-zone wafers for leak-free arrays
idea: Particle detectors use float-zone silicon grown without a quartz crucible, with ~100x less oxygen and few oxygen-vacancy traps. Develop 300 mm float-zone (or crucible-free pedestal-grown) substrates for DRAM array wafers so oxygen-precipitate generation centers near the access junction are gone.
why: Resources and fact 3: removes the Spruce Pine high-purity-quartz crucible dependency for array wafers and shrinks the retention tail; 300 mm FZ growth is unproven and oxygen-free wafers lose some mechanical strength.

title: Substitute beamline implant with self-assembled monolayer doping on 3D channels
idea: Substitute ion implantation (whose plasma flood guns run on argon or xenon) with monolayer doping. Phosphorus- or boron-bearing molecules self-assemble on exposed Si sidewalls from solution, are capped with oxide, and are driven in by semiconductor diode-laser spike heating, forming a conformal, damage-free, sub-5 nm junction even on the lateral channels of 3D DRAM tiers.
why: No implant damage, which removes a main source of tail-leakage traps, and conformal doping of stacked lateral transistors, a 3D DRAM blocker.

title: Thymic negative-selection screening catches variable-retention cells continuously
idea: Like the thymus, which deletes T cells that react to self-antigens under stress, the controller uses idle time to test a rotating slice of rows under stress (doubled refresh interval, worst-case coupling patterns), flags rows whose cells flip in a small on-die 'antibody' table, and runs every unflagged row at 4x relaxed refresh.
why: Continuous screening makes retention-aware refresh safe against variable-retention-time cells that change over life, giving ~70-75% fewer refreshes plus the matching energy and bandwidth gain.

title: Atlas one-level store: lifetime-tagged pages that never get refreshed
idea: Revive the 1962 Manchester Atlas one-level store, whose hardware page tables tracked residency: add a lifetime-class bit to page-table entries and to the memory controller. Tensors rewritten faster than the retention time (activations, gradient buffers, ring buffers) go into rows marked no-refresh, and the OS guarantees each is rewritten within the certified retention time.
why: Short-lived AI data can be a large share of training memory; skipping refresh for it cuts refresh energy and the bandwidth tax roughly in proportion (fact 3), with no device change.

title: OS compacts live pages into best-retention rows before self-refresh
idea: Po: the best cells do all the work. On entering idle, the OS migrates live pages into rows profiled as the top-decile retention class and powers the rest down with partial-array self-refresh, so the self-refresh interval is set by the best rows, not the worst.
why: Fact 3 idle power: best-decile rows retain ~10x longer than the worst, so standby refresh power in phones and edge boxes drops up to ~10x.

title: Substitute raw data storage with leakage-minimizing per-row polarity coding
idea: Substitute raw data with a per-row inversion flag chosen at write time so most cells sit in their discharged, non-leaking state (true-cell/anti-cell layout included). The row's charged-cell count is stored, and rows with few charged cells are refreshed at a relaxed rate.
why: On average halves the number of cells exposed to leakage; with ECC margin, 1.5-2x less refresh from a pure controller/DRAM-logic change.

title: In-field electrothermal annealing heals leaky tail cells
idea: IFR: weak cells repair themselves. The controller locates tail cells by retention scan, then drives a controlled microsecond current pulse through that wordline segment (local ~300-400 C) so mobile hydrogen re-passivates the trap sites near the storage junction that cause trap-assisted GIDL.
why: Fact 3: the <=13 fA tail sets refresh for the whole chip; healing the worst ~0.01% of cells could stretch the refresh interval from 64 ms to 256 ms or more, ~4x less refresh energy and bandwidth.

title: Lopsided access transistor: wide-gap storage-side contact kills GIDL
idea: Inverts 'the access transistor is symmetric': replace only the storage-node-side source/drain extension with a thin wide-gap oxide semiconductor contact, so the gate-to-storage overlap, where GIDL band-to-band tunneling dominates, sits in a >3 eV material while the bitline side stays silicon for drive current.
why: BTBT falls exponentially with bandgap, so storage-side GIDL drops ~100x and the tail (fact 3) shrinks enough for ~4-8x longer refresh.

title: Minify grain to one domain: wall-free ferroelectric nanodots for fatigue immunity
idea: Pattern HZO into <=8 nm epitaxial single-domain islands on a templated seed so each switches coherently without domain-wall nucleation or pinning, removing the defect-redistribution paths behind wake-up and fatigue; arrays of dots form each cell capacitor.
why: Targets FeRAM endurance from ~1e11 to >1e15 for a non-volatile DRAM replacement; tighter switching distribution also lowers voltage.

title: Photon-emission retention mapping fuses per-row internal refresh bins
idea: Effect: junction and hot-carrier electroluminescence. At sort the array is biased to stress leakage paths and a cooled InGaAs camera images the faint NIR emission; leaky row segments glow, so a weak-row map is captured in seconds instead of hours of retention testing and burned into fuses; the die then refreshes strong rows only every 4th REF. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3): -50-75%; optics resolve row segments, not single cells, which is enough for row binning.

title: Geologist's squeezed crystal: piezoelectronic access transistor
idea: A geologist knows squeezing certain crystals turns insulators into metals. Each access switch is a piezoelectronic transistor: a thin PMN-PT actuator driven at ~0.15 V compresses a SmSe pressure-driven insulator-metal layer between bitline and storage node, switching it in acoustic-transit time, with a wide-gap blocking layer in series to reach DRAM-grade off-resistance.
why: A 0.1-0.2 V gate versus a 3 V pumped wordline cuts wordline CV^2 ~100x, targeting >10x lower total access energy; on/off ratio and fatigue are the big unknowns.

title: Crosspoint 1S1C with wide-gap punch-through selector, eight layers
idea: IFR: the cell needs no third terminal. Stack eight DUV-patterned crosspoint layers, each cell a MIM capacitor in series with a symmetric n-p-n punch-through selector in a wide-gap oxide engineered for <1e-19 A at V/3 half-select bias and steep turn-on above ~1.5 V; reads are destructive with write-back, as in DRAM.
why: Constraint: 4F^2 per layer x 8 layers versus 6F^2 is ~12x density, and each layer needs ~2 non-EUV masks, holding wafer cost near today's EUV-heavy DRAM.

title: Minify the switching volume: hidden-state Mott charge-density-wave bits
idea: Exploit the metastable 'hidden' metallic state of 1T-TaS2 (strain-engineered to stay stable above room temperature): a 10 ns current pulse switches a nanoflake between insulating CDW and metastable metallic order with 10-100x resistance contrast that persists unpowered.
why: Electronic rather than ionic switching promises unlimited endurance and sub-pJ writes; room-temperature stability is the open question.
